title: The Criterion Collection
subtitle: every spine number, in order
blurb: Spines #1 to #1337 — 1337 releases, about 2313 hours, each with the formats Criterion put it out on.
notes: Sorted by spine number, because that is the collection.

Criterion numbers every release, and the number is how the collection is referred to. The numbering restarted at 1 when the line moved from LaserDisc to DVD in 1998, so these are the DVD-era numbers — #1 is Grand Illusion, #1337 is The Right Stuff.
Formats are what Criterion lists now, plus LaserDisc.

DVD, Blu-ray and 4K are read off each film's own Criterion page, and count an edition whether it is sold on its own or only inside a box set. The catch is that Criterion delists an edition once it goes out of print: #1 Grand Illusion had a Blu-ray in 2012 and its page no longer mentions it, so it shows here as LaserDisc and DVD. Read these as what you can still get hold of rather than as a complete pressing history. LaserDisc is the exception — it comes from Wikipedia, which is the only place that history survives. Counts across the collection: Blu-ray 1036, DVD 924, LaserDisc 293, 4K 213.
LaserDisc-only releases are their own section.

81 films Criterion put out on LaserDisc and never reissued. They carry the old numbering, which collides with the DVD numbering above, so mixing them into one sequence would produce two #2s and two #4s. They sit outside a finish date unless you tick the box under the bar.
Ivan the Terrible, Part I and Part II share one number. Every other spine in the list is one entry.
Read from each film's own Criterion page. 172 of the 1337 have no runtime listed and weigh nothing, so they cannot drag a group's pace.
Catalogue, editions and runtimes from criterion.com; LaserDisc history from Wikipedia's List of films in the Criterion Collection.

sections.sub: 81 releases · a separate numbering, out of print since the nineties
sections.intro: Criterion's LaserDisc line ran from 1984 to 1998 and had its own spine numbers, which were reset when the DVD line began. These are the releases that never made the jump, so their numbers overlap unrelated films above. Nothing here is purchasable; a finish date skips them unless you tick the box under the bar.
